title: Gradio FileExplorer -- T1005 os.path.join root_dir prefix discard path traversal
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-49119 (CVSS 8.7 HIGH), affecting
Gradio before 6.16.0.

The `FileExplorer` component's `preprocess()` method joined caller-
supplied path segments with `os.path.join(self.root_dir, *segments)`
followed by `os.path.normpath()`. Two ways this fails to confine the
result to `root_dir`: an ABSOLUTE path segment (e.g. `["/etc/passwd"]`)
causes `os.path.join` to discard the `root_dir` prefix entirely (a
well-known Python `os.path.join` footgun), and a `..`-laden segment
list (e.g. `["..", "..", "etc", "passwd"]`) resolves outside root via
normal traversal. Either shape lets an unauthenticated caller read
arbitrary files reachable by the server process, outside the directory
the component's configuration was meant to confine them to.

Detection logic flags a request to a FileExplorer-backed endpoint whose
path-segment parameter is either an absolute path or contains a `..`
traversal component -- the two shapes the advisory's own fix
specifically targets by switching to the already-safe `_safe_join()`
helper (the same one the component's `ls()` endpoint already used).

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor fix (gradio-app/gradio, via the
merged PR and VulnCheck's corroborating write-up), fixed in 6.16.0.
